dedupe_keys.name: a deep learning approach for rapid detection of soil liquefaction using time frequency images

description: A deep learning approach for rapid detection of soil liquefaction using time-frequency images is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Wenyang Zhang, University of Texas at Austin (utexas.edu). In this project, we utilize a convolutional neural network (CNN), with the help of time-frequency images of surface accelerations, to predict both the occurrence of a liquefaction event and its triggering time (if it occurred). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: Liquefaction, deep learning, convolutional neural network, time-frequency images. Published 2023-01-26. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
